video.title: Cameron Boozer or AJ Dybantsa? Ranking The 2026 NBA Rookies

summary: Josh Lloyd finishes his 2026 dynasty rookie rankings with the top 12, giving separate lists for points leagues (Yahoo default scoring) and category leagues. In points leagues, the top four picks of the draft make up tier one: Cameron Boozer 1, AJ Dybantsa 2, Darryn Peterson 3, Caleb Wilson 4. In category leagues he has Boozer 1, Peterson 2 and Wilson 3, then drops Dybantsa to 4 because of weak threes, steals, blocks and free throws. He says you should take Boozer first in every dynasty draft. He also walks through the four point guard tier (Wagler, Brown, Flemings, Acuff), Charlotte's crowded center rotation after its trades, and which players he ranks above or below their draft slots.

rules.text: Points league advice can mislead because default scoring differs between platforms. Yahoo default does not penalize missed shots. ESPN boosts threes, takes points off for misses and weights defensive stats more. Sleeper counts ejections and technical fouls.
rules.quote: Do you mean the Yahoo default scoring where shot efficiency doesn't matter? There's no penalty for missed shots.

rules.text: For dynasty rookie rankings, judge players over roughly a 4 to 6 year window, not 1 year and not 12.
rules.quote: I'm looking at probably a let's say 4-6 year window of like this is the level of production

rules.text: His rankings mix statistical translation with scouting, draft capital and age.
rules.quote: It then gets tied into scouting. It gets tied into draft capital. It gets tied into age.

rules.text: Players in the same tier are close in value, so you can order them however you like. Weigh how likely each one is to become a 30 minute a night player long term, plus his stats and his team.
rules.quote: You got to take how do you view the players, their propensity to be a 30 minute a night guy long term.

rules.text: Year one and year two playing time adds dynasty value. A rookie who lands somewhere with immediate minutes ranks much higher than one stuck behind a deep rotation.
rules.quote: Because you get year one, year two production.

rules.text: Being the number one overall pick does not make a player the top dynasty fantasy asset. Many number one picks have disappointed.
rules.quote: just because he went number one doesn't mean that he has to be the number one or number two fantasy dynasty guy

rules.text: To spot breakouts among non point guards, look for assist rate and free throw rate climbing over the first six years. That is how a player around 40th overall becomes a top 10 player.
rules.quote: can you envisage or or will you see assist rate climbing over the first 6 years?

rules.text: A free throw rate jump from about 4 attempts to 6.5 or 7 per game can move a player from around 25th to around 5th.
rules.quote: six and a half to seven free throw attempts per game instead of four. That's that's the jump from 25 to five.

rules.text: Rookie guards usually struggle a lot with efficiency and turnovers early on.
rules.quote: He's going to be like every rookie guard struggle a lot with efficiency and turnovers early on.

rules.text: Do not tweak your ranking formula just to match a gut feeling. Present the data, then give your subjective view separately.
rules.quote: I'm not going to go in and adjust the formula that I use to put him clearly sitting in tier one.

rules.text: High usage, volume scorers are worth more in Yahoo points leagues than in category leagues, where efficiency, assists, steals and blocks matter more.
rules.quote: If you want to take efficiency and you know, big ramp up of assists and block and steal numbers, he's not as effective.
